The Nancy Gardner Sewell Act (S.339) allocates Medicare funds for multi-cancer screening tests starting in 2028, pegging payment rates to existing stool DNA tests ($500-$600 per test). While early detection matters, this bill codifies D.C.’s addiction to blank-check healthcare spending without addressing systemic bloat.

Section 2(b)(2) imposes arbitrary age restrictions (68+ in 2028, escalating yearly), denying younger seniors access despite cancer risks. Worse, Section 2(a)(1)(C) lets HHS bureaucrats unilaterally define “appropriate” coverage parameters—a recipe for mission creep.

Medicare already hemorrhages $900B annually. Adding $1.2B+ for unproven MCED tests without auditing existing oncology waste (like $2.4B in annual Medicare fraud) isn’t reform—it’s fiscal malpractice.
